title: Creating encounters: Generations in Action – Together Instead of Alone (GemsE)
summary: Older people and children from families with mentally ill parents are particularly affected by loneliness. The GemsE project is investigating whether intergenerational mentoring between seniors and children or young people helps to reduce loneliness and improve the mental well-being and quality of life of both groups. The aim of the study is to scientifically record the effect of these sponsorships and to find out how such encounters can be successfully organized.
conditions: Children and adolescents between the ages of 12 and 21 with at least one parent suffering from mental illness, as well as older people aged 60 and above who suffer from loneliness and psychosocial stress.

interventions.name:
Establishing intergenerational mentoring relationships

The intervention focuses on establishing stable mentoring relationships between senior citizens and children or adolescents from families with parents who have mental health issues.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Seniors aged 60 and over who are residents of Hamburg
- Children and adolescents aged 12-21 who have a parent with a mental illness and are residents of Hamburg
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language - Consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Children and adolescents with severe acute psychological symptoms, such as acute suicidality, acute substance use, or acute psychotic symptoms, which indicate inpatient treatment, are excluded from participating in the study. Seniors with acute psychological crises or untreated severe mental illnesses, as well as cognitive impairments or dementia, which do not allow for reliable participation in the intervention, are also excluded.
